errors.save_failed.context: A save attempt has failed; success has not been reported.
errors.save_failed.note: Do not add a promise about draft recovery unless it is supported.

errors.comet_failed.context: The app has confirmed that the comet was not sent.
errors.comet_failed.note: Use this wording only when delivery failure is known.

errors.world_unavailable.note: Give an available route back into the universe.

empty.no_world.context: A person has not created their own world yet.
empty.no_world.note: An invitation to begin, with one clear action.

empty.no_comets.context: The owner’s world has no received comets.
empty.no_comets.note: Explain the feature without treating a quiet world as a failure.

empty.comet_composer.context: A visitor opens the comet composer before writing a message.
empty.comet_composer.note: Keep the field label visible. Enable sending once the message is valid.

celebrations.world_created.context: The first world has been created and saved successfully.
celebrations.world_created.note: Celebrate the beginning without adding a list of tasks.

celebrations.first_comet.context: The world has received its first comet.
celebrations.first_comet.note: Celebrate the gesture, not a popularity score.

celebrations.new_moon.context: A bloom event has actually added a moon to the world.
celebrations.new_moon.note: Name the visible change. Do not imply that every bloom adds a moon.

notifications.welcome.note: A welcoming subject with no demand to finish onboarding.

notifications.comet_arrived.context: Push title after a comet has arrived on the recipient’s world.
notifications.comet_arrived.note: Send only after the event. The subject does not quote the visitor’s message.

notifications.new_moon.context: Email subject or push title after a moon has been added.
notifications.new_moon.note: The event provides the reason to return. Do not add false urgency.
